extracted.intended_audience: readers, editors, and scholars of Edmund Burke; general readers of 18th‑century political philosophy and aesthetics
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and exemplars related to aesthetic and philosophical criticism (the sublime and the beautiful) together with editorial/publishing and redistribution standards found in the prefatory material and license of an edited edition of Burke's works.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rectify errors of the press
rubrics_metrics.description: Such errors of the press as have been discovered in it are here rectified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing an edition, correct discovered printing errors against reliable sources; preserve meaning while fixing printing mistakes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve chronological arrangement where practicable
rubrics_metrics.description: In other respects it is faithfully followed, except that in one instance an accident of little moment has occasioned a slight deviation from the strict chronological arrangement...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain strict chronological order for collected works unless a clear, minor justification exists to deviate; prefer chronological context for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Insert speeches and pieces in their proper place
rubrics_metrics.description: a speech of conspicuous excellence... is here, for the first time, inserted in its proper place.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place items (speeches, letters) in the edition where they best fit historically and thematically rather than leaving them out or misplacing them for convenience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Omit ephemeral prefaces and only preserve necessary explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: The several posthumous publications, as they from time to time made their appearance, were accompanied by appropriate prefaces. These, however, as they were principally intended for temporary purposes, have been omitted. Some few explanations only, which they contained, seem here to be necessary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exclude temporary or narrowly‑purpose prefaces when assembling collected works; retain only explanatory notes that add lasting value or necessary context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect authorial responsibility when reconstructing posthumous material
rubrics_metrics.description: Care has been taken not to attribute to Mr. Burke any sentiment which is not most explicitly known, from repeated conversations, and from much correspondence, to have been decidedly entertained by that illustrious man.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When editing incomplete or posthumous manuscripts, avoid attributing statements or sentiments to the author unless supported by explicit evidence; use discretion and document editorial interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: When manuscripts are imperfect, use limited editorial discretion for subordinate points
rubrics_metrics.description: No important change, none at all affecting the meaning of any passage, has been made in either, though in the more imperfect parcel some latitude of discretion in subordinate points was necessarily used.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow minimal, clearly defensible adjustments to structure or wording in fragmentary drafts, but avoid substantive changes to meaning; note such interventions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standardize orthography by author's consistency or best authorities
rubrics_metrics.description: The rule laid down for the discharge of this task was, that, whenever Mr. Burke could be perceived to have been uniform in his mode of spelling, that was considered as decisive; but where he varied... the best received authorities were directed to be followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For historical texts, keep an author's consistent spelling; where the author varies, adopt standard or authoritative contemporary spellings to aid readability while documenting choices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Compare quotations with original authors
rubrics_metrics.description: The quotations which are interspersed through the works of Mr Burke... have been generally compared with the original authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Verify and, if necessary, correct quoted passages by checking original sources to prevent error and preserve accuracy of citations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Correct misprints that pervert or obscure sense
rubrics_metrics.description: Several mistakes in printing, of one word for another, by which the sense was either perverted or obscured, are now rectified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identify and fix typographical errors that change meaning; document corrections in notes or errata.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preserve and cautiously use authorial marks indicating insertions
rubrics_metrics.description: Two or three small insertions have also been made from a quarto copy corrected by Mr. Burke himself... Several other parts... were indicated in the same manner; but, as they in general consist of single sentences, and as the meaning of the mark by which they were distinguished was not actually expressed, it has not been thought necessary to notice them particularly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Respect marginalia and authorial marks as possible indications of intended insertions but avoid speculative insertion without clear intent; record uncertainty in editorial notes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Arrange volumes for methodical balance
rubrics_metrics.description: A different distribution of the contents... has, at the same time, been fortunately found to produce a more methodical arrangement of the whole.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In multi‑volume editions, distribute material to balance bulk and create a logical, methodical arrangement that improves usability for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid altering principles or meaning to suppress controversy
rubrics_metrics.description: To have passed it over in silent neglect, on the one hand, or, on the other, to have then made any considerable changes in it, might have seemed an abandonment of the principles which it contained.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When controversial works are published or reissued, do not alter arguments or major content to avoid controversy; preserve the author's principles and contextualize them instead.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluate propositions by truth, not by feared consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: Error... is dangerous; that ill conclusions can only flow from false propositions; and that, to know whether any proposition be true or false, it is a preposterous method to examine it by its apparent consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess philosophical or argumentative claims on their truth and internal coherence rather than judging them solely by hypothetical outcomes or perceived dangers of inquiry.

rubrics_metrics.name: Beware of specious plausibility and rhetorical seduction
rubrics_metrics.description: There is a sort of gloss upon ingenious falsehoods that dazzles the imagination, but which neither belongs to, nor becomes the sober aspect of truth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Distinguish plausibility from sound argument; treat rhetorically striking reasoning with scepticism and seek substantive proof rather than being won by style alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prefer comprehensive, original materials and deep survey to superficial reasoning
rubrics_metrics.description: When we must seek in a profound subject, not only for arguments, but for new materials of argument, their measures and their method of arrangement; when we must go out of the sphere of our ordinary ideas...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth inquiry should rely on original evidence and broad consideration rather than on commonplace experience or facile analogies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not suppress fair discussion to avoid dangerous consequences
rubrics_metrics.description: They argue against a fair discussion of popular prejudices, because... the discovery might be productive of the most dangerous consequences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allow open examination of popular beliefs even when arguments might challenge them; censorship of inquiry on grounds of possible social danger is condemned.

rubrics_metrics.name: Temper extravagant imagination with natural/bodily restraint
rubrics_metrics.description: Enough has not been said upon the restraint which our bodily necessities ought to lay on the extravagant sublimities and eccentric rovings of our minds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When producing imaginative or philosophical writing, balance lofty speculation with grounding in ordinary human needs and practical considerations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Two‑part viewpoint for political judgement (external and internal)
rubrics_metrics.description: In looking over any state to form a judgment on it, it presents itself in two lights; the external... and the internal... the relation which its component parts, the governing and the governed, bear to each other.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess states or political bodies both by their foreign relations and by their internal governance and social relations; both dimensions are necessary for a full judgment.

rubrics_metrics.guidance: When sharing Project Gutenberg texts, include the exact required sentence with active access to the full license to comply with distribution terms.

Do not copy, display, perform, distribute or redistribute this electronic work... without prominently displaying the sentence set forth in paragraph 1.E.1... (1.E.4, 1.E.5)

rubrics_metrics.name: Provide original 'Plain Vanilla ASCII' or means to obtain it if distributing alternate formats

Any alternate format must include the full Project Gutenberg License. (1.E.6)

rubrics_metrics.name: Do not charge fees for Project Gutenberg works except under specified royalty/refund conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Do not charge a fee for access to, viewing, displaying, performing, copying or distributing any Project Gutenberg works unless you comply with paragraph 1.E.8 or 1.E.9. (1.E.7)
